findings.title: `queued` default is evaluated once at import time
findings.body: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is a dataclass default, so `timezone.now()` runs once when the module is imported. Every `AssignmentSource` created in the process then gets the same stale timestamp rather than the time the assignment was queued. The field is serialized into the task payload, so the recorded time is wrong. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` instead.

findings.title: to_dict() returns a datetime that is passed into Celery task kwargs
findings.body: `to_dict()` uses `asdict(self)`, which keeps `queued` as a `datetime` object. `sync_group_assignee_outbound` passes this dict as `assignment_source_dict` in `apply_async` kwargs. If the task serializer is JSON, which is the usual setup, enqueuing fails with a TypeError on every assignment that carries an assignment source, such as every inbound Jira/integration assignment. The outbound sync would then break for exactly the path this PR touches. Serialize `queued` to an ISO string (and parse it back in `from_dict`), or drop it from the payload.

findings.title: from_dict does not restore `queued` to a datetime and accepts any value
findings.body: `from_dict` passes the dict straight into the constructor, so a `queued` value round-tripped through JSON comes back as a string, not a datetime. The annotation `datetime` is then wrong for any consumer that reads it. Also, the broad `(ValueError, TypeError)` handling silently turns malformed payloads into `None`, which hides the loss of the loop-prevention context.

findings.title: Tests do not cover the serialization round trip used by the Celery task
findings.body: `test_to_dict` only checks that `queued` is not None, and no test runs `from_dict(to_dict())` or passes the dict through a JSON round trip. That is the path used by `sync_group_assignee_outbound` and `sync_assignee_outbound`, and it is where the datetime serialization problem would show up.

findings.title: No test covers the deassign path with a matching assignment source
findings.body: The loop fix is tested only for `assign`. The `deassign` path, which also now accepts `assignment_source` and forwards it to the outbound sync, has no test checking that an inbound unassign from integration X skips outbound sync to X. The inbound deassign flow in `sync_group_assignee_inbound` is therefore untested for the cycle-breaking behaviour the PR is meant to provide.
